item.content:encoded: Der österreichische Versicherungskonzern Vienna Insurance Group (VIG) (VIGR.VI) hat seinen Gewinn im ersten Halbjahr dank eines starken Osteuropa-Geschäfts und guter Kapitalanlageergebnisse kräftig gesteigert. Das Ergebnis vor Steuern kletterte um rund ein Fünftel auf 641,5 Millionen Euro, wie das Unternehmen am Mittwoch mitteilte. Die verrechneten Prämien legten um 5,4 Prozent auf 9,03 Milliarden Euro zu. Dank geringerer Schäden verbesserte sich die Schaden-Kosten-Quote auf 91,4 von 91,9 Prozent. Gestiegene Marktwerte ließen zudem das Kapitalanlageportfolio um 4,1 Prozent auf 49,1 Milliarden Euro anwachsen. Für 2026 bekräftigte das Management die Prognose eines Vorsteuergewinns von 1,25 bis 1,30 Milliarden Euro. In diesem Ausblick ist die im Mai übernommene Nürnberger Versicherung noch nicht enthalten. Sie fließt aber in den Jahresabschluss ein. Der rund 1,4 Milliarden Euro teure Zukauf – die größte Transaktion der Firmengeschichte – drückte die Solvenzquote im Vergleich zu Ende 2025 zwar auf 272 von 296 Prozent, doch die Kapitalausstattung bleibt damit hoch. Die Nürnberger stärke die Diversifikation in Deutschland, erklärte Konzernchef Hartwig Löger. Fokus der Integration sei nun die IT. In den Kernmärkten in Mittel- und Osteuropa wuchs die VIG fast überall, vor allem in Polen, Tschechien und Ungarn. Nur in der Türkei drosselte der Konzern das Kfz-Haftpflichtgeschäft zur Sicherung der Profitabilität.

item.title: European shares edge higher as oil falls; Nvidia earnings in focus
item.description: European shares edged higher on Wednesday as a drop in oil prices dragged bond yields lower on hopes that the Strait of Hormuz may reopen soon, while investors braced for an earnings report from AI bellwether Nvidia.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: European shares edged higher on Wednesday as a drop in oil prices dragged bond yields lower on hopes that the Strait of Hormuz may reopen soon, while investors braced for an earnings report from AI bellwether Nvidia. The pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) was up 0.1% at 657.34, as of 0703 GMT, with basic resources (.SXPP) leading sectoral gains, up 0.9%. Iran said it had [USN:L8N44M1SQ TEXT:"restarted talks"] with Oman on managing the Strait of Hormuz amid mounting pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump in the nearly six-month conflict that has roiled oil markets and stoked global inflationary worries. Brent crude futures fell for a third straight day, dropping more than 2% to around $86 a barrel on prospects of increased oil flows through Hormuz, helping drive bond yields lower. The energy index (.SXEP) fell 1.1% and was the worst performing sector on the STOXX 600. item.content:encoded: Die Norddeutsche Landesbank (NordLB) hat ihren Vorsteuergewinn im ersten Halbjahr um 40 Prozent gesteigert. Das operative Ergebnis kletterte auf 370 Millionen Euro, wie das Institut aus Hannover am Mittwoch mitteilte. Unterm Strich stieg der Konzerngewinn um rund 46 Prozent auf 309 Millionen Euro. Die Bank habe ihren erfolgreichen Kurs der vergangenen Jahre fortgesetzt, sagte Vorstandschef Jörg Frischholz. "Besonders erfreulich ist, dass wir unsere Profitabilität erneut gesteigert haben und unseren mittelfristigen Zielen damit ein weiteres Stück nähergekommen sind." Für das Gesamtjahr bleibt die NordLB(NDLG.UL) vorsichtig optimistisch und will die 475 Millionen Euro Vorsteuergewinn von 2025 übertreffen. Nach der ersten Jahreshälfte hat die Bank schon fast 80 Prozent dieses Ziels erreicht. Das Institut steigerte die Eigenkapitalrendite (RoE) vor Steuern auf 9,0 Prozent, nach 7,0 Prozent vor Jahresfrist. Das Zinsergebnis legte um sieben Prozent zu, während der Provisionsüberschuss um 26 Prozent zunahm. "Wichtige Impulse kamen insbesondere aus dem Neugeschäft im Bereich der strukturierten Finanzierungen", sagte Finanzchef Jasper Hanebuth. Positiv niedergeschlagen hätten sich auch der Ausbau des Einlagengeschäfts und sogenanntes Ausplatzieren - also Verkauf oder Weitergabe von Finanzinstrumenten, Krediten oder Wertpapieren an andere Banken oder Investoren. Bei der NordLB steht ein endgültiger Schlussstrich unter Rettung und Umbau der Landesbank bevor. Nach Milliardenverlusten durch faule Schiffskredite musste sie Ende 2019 mit einer Kapitalspritze von 3,6 Milliarden Euro gerettet werden. In die Bresche sprangen damals neben den Alt-Eigentümern auch die bundesweiten Sparkassen und Landesbanken mit rund 757 Millionen Euro. Diese wollen nun mit Ende der Stützung wieder aussteigen, verlautete es im Umfeld der Bank. Gespräche dazu laufen. Niedersachsen will diese Anteile von knapp 24 Prozent übernehmen und könnte dann mit fast 82 Prozent durchregieren, weil für wichtige Beschlüsse eine 80-Prozent-Mehrheit nötig ist. Dafür müsste das Land per Nachtragshaushalt einen Kredit aufnehmen, könnte aber mit einer Dividende wohl die erste Tranche zahlen, heißt es im politischen Hannover.

item.title: El IBEX 35 sube a la espera de Nvidia y el PCE estadounidense
item.description: El índice español IBEX 35 abría la sesión del miércoles al alza, en un clima de expectativa en los inversores por los resultados de Nvidia , centrando su atención en si el enorme auge del gasto en inteligencia artificial es sostenible y puede generar ganancias que satisfagan a los mercados.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El índice español IBEX 35 (.IBEX) abría la sesión del miércoles al alza, en un clima de expectativa en los inversores por los resultados de Nvidia (NVDA.O) , centrando su atención en si el enorme auge del gasto en inteligencia artificial es sostenible y puede generar ganancias que satisfagan a los mercados. "Como empresa de mayor capitalización a nivel global y uno de los grandes protagonistas en la IA, más que los resultados, que se esperan excelentes (BPA +98,7% hasta 2,09$), sus guías y comentarios servirán para dar dirección a un sector que, tras una carrera impresionante en el año (semis +64%), muestra altibajos recientemente y cae en el trimestre -19%", dijeron los analistas de Bankinter en su canal de Telegram. Los mercados también aguardaban por la publicación del índice de precios de los Gastos de Consumo Personal (PCE, por sus siglas en inglés) de Estados Unidos correspondiente a julio, que se conocerá a las 1230 GMT, además del discurso que pronunciará el viernes el presidente de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, en el simposio del banco central en Jackson Hole, para conseguir referencias sobre la trayectoria futura de los tipos de interés en EEUU. "La sesión estará muy parada hasta la macro americana a mediodía… y si no hay sorpresas por ahí, quizá hasta conocer los resultados de Nvidia, que ya serán tras el cierre. No esperemos mucho hoy", agregaron en Bankinter. A las 0705 GMT, el selectivo bursátil español IBEX 35 subía 55,30 puntos, un 0,28%, hasta 20.111,90 puntos, mientras que el índice de grandes valores europeos FTSE Eurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) avanzaba un 0,14%. En el sector bancario, Santander (SAN.MC) subía un 1,00%, BBVA (BBVA.MC) se anotaba un 0,85%, Caixabank (CABK.MC) cedía un 0,11%, Sabadell (SABE.MC) caía un 0,16%, Bankinter (BKT.MC) se dejaba un 0,06% y Unicaja Banco (UNI.MC) subía un 0,11%. Entre los grandes valores no financieros, Telefónica (TEF.MC) retrocedía un 0,35%, Inditex (ITX.MC) avanzaba un 0,27%, Iberdrola (IBE.MC) se revalorizaba un 0,10%, Cellnex (CLNX.MC) caía un 0,22% y la petrolera Repsol (REP.MC) perdía un 1,49%. Entre el resto de las eléctricas, Naturgy (NTGY.MC) retrocedía un 0,53%, mientras Endesa (ELE.MC) cedía un 0,12%.

item.content:encoded: Der südkoreanische Autobauer Hyundai Motor (005380.KS) will mit einer umfassenden Produktoffensive und höheren Gewinnzielen seine Position auf dem Weltmarkt ausbauen. Bis 2030 solle die Produktionskapazität um 1,27 Millionen Einheiten erweitert werden, kündigte der Konzern am Mittwoch an. Zudem sollen weltweit mehr als 100 Modelle neu auf den Markt kommen oder überarbeitet werden, mehr als die Hälfte davon in Nordamerika. Das Unternehmen strebe eine operative Gewinnmarge von über neun Prozent an. An der Börse kamen die Pläne jedoch nicht gut an: Die Aktie des Konzerns fiel um 2,8 Prozent, während der Leitindex Kospi (.KS11) um 1,3 Prozent zulegte. "Unsere Fundamentaldaten waren noch nie so stark", sagte Konzernchef Jose Munoz. Zu den neuen Modellen gehöre eine Version des Santa Fe als Elektrofahrzeug mit Reichweitenverlängerer (EREV) und ein Hybridmodell im Luxussegment. Hyundai, zusammen mit der Schwesterfirma Kia (000270.KS) der drittgrößte Autobauer der Welt, wolle damit auch in Segmenten Fuß fassen, in denen die Marke bislang unterrepräsentiert sei. Der Vorstand kündigte zudem an, eigene Aktien im Wert von rund 789 Milliarden Won (etwa 489 Millionen Euro) einzuziehen und eine Ausschüttungsquote von mindestens 35 Prozent beizubehalten. Die Expansionspläne in den USA stehen jedoch unter dem Vorbehalt der laufenden Überprüfung des Handelsabkommens zwischen den USA, Mexiko und Kanada (USMCA).

item.title: Australia transport safety regulator probes two more incidents at Sydney airport
item.description: Australia's transport safety regulator on Wednesday opened two investigations into taxiing conflicts at Sydney airport, involving a Virgin and Qantas aircraft on August 16 and a Jetstar and Bombardier aircraft on August 25.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Australia's transport safety regulator on Wednesday opened two investigations into taxiing conflicts at Sydney airport, involving a Virgin (VGN.AX) and Qantas (QAN.AX) aircraft on August 16 and a Jetstar and Bombardier aircraft on August 25. The Australian Transport Safety Bureau (ATSB) classified both events as safety incidents rather than serious incidents, saying there was no immediate risk of collision as flight and ground crews reacted to avoid conflict. On August 16, a taxiing Virgin 737 was told by air traffic control to give way to a Qantas 737 vacating the runway. The instruction was not read back correctly and went unnoticed by controllers, the ATSB said in a statement. On August 25, incomplete traffic information was passed to a Jetstar A320, creating a conflict with a taxiing Bombardier Dash 8. The two investigations are being run separately but with coordinating teams, and could be widened or combined depending on the evidence. The ATSB expects to publish preliminary reports on both investigations within six to eight weeks. Virgin and Qantas, which also owns Jetstar, said in separate statements they will support the ATSB's investigations. The regulator is already investigating [USN:L4N44I02N TEXT:"four similar incidents"] at the airport, including one that injured a member of a plane's cabin crew.

item.title: Bill Gates, alarmed by AI, has policy ideas he wants to discuss with China's Xi
item.description: Bill Gates is looking to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping later this year, eager to propose global efforts to mitigate the growing risks posed by artificial intelligence.
item.dc:creator: Jeffrey Dastin
item.content:encoded: Bill Gates is looking to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping later this year, eager to propose global efforts to mitigate the growing risks posed by artificial intelligence. The Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist told Reuters in an interview that he believes China might agree to restricting potentially dangerous AI model releases if the U.S. took initiative on that first. "The whole world would go along with that," said Gates, who met with Xi [USN:B9N381078 TEXT:"three years ago"], when he was the first foreign entrepreneur to be hosted by the Chinese president post-pandemic. Gates also said he'd like to propose that countries monitor AI's ability to create molecules and carry out biological attacks — something that would not get in the way of any tech industry's development. Gates' staff are working to finalize a meeting with Xi for his next China trip, his spokesperson said, scheduled tentatively for November. President Xi "might be surprised by how vehement I am," Gates said. He said China is protecting children from AI companion addiction, but he believes few leaders globally are rising to the occasion to get ahead of a litany of potential harms from AI. "Yes, in the past, technology never did this. This time is different. This is like an evolutionary milestone that needs incredible policy management by society as a whole." China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment. AI HACKING 'SHOULD BLOW PEOPLE'S MINDS' Gates struck [USN:L6N3YO0OR TEXT:"a more optimistic note"] about AI in January, but since then he has become concerned that it can conduct attacks while supplanting jobs and hooking users psychologically. For instance, technology from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta Platforms (META.O) recently hacked real-world websites in what were supposed to be [USN:L4N43W34R TEXT:"isolated"] [USN:L6N43Q12M TEXT:"cybersecurity evaluations"]. "These security incidents are shocking, and they should blow people's minds," Gates said. In a blog post on Wednesday, Gates called for a new international organization to manage AI, drawing on elements from a nuclear inspections regime, international aviation regulations, and ozone layer protection agreements. To date, U.S. President Donald Trump's administration has exercised some control over the distribution of powerful AI models such as Anthropic’s Fable 5, but more regulation has taken place at the state level. Whereas many tech leaders have, like Meta [USN:L1N447029 TEXT:"CEO Mark Zuckerberg"], touted the benefits of AI, many have also expressed concern about its perils. Demis Hassabis, chair of Google DeepMind (GOOGL.O) , proposed a body like the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority, or FINRA, that could develop and conduct tests of AI related to national security. Gates agrees with others that the United States should take the lead, but says it must establish what criteria would determine what action. "You can use a FINRA-type model, but it's a silly conversation," Gates said. "It’s like saying, ‘Should we meet to discuss taxation at this restaurant or this restaurant?'" ‘WORLD’S TOP PRIORITY’ In his blog post, Gates said it was the “world’s top priority” to deliver an AI future that does not widen inequality and hurt the vulnerable, ahead of climate change and health crises. As he pursues high-profile engagements, Gates also told Reuters he planned to see UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham this autumn. In February, he cancelled an appearance in India after the U.S. released files from sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Gates has said he [USN:L1N42H0HT TEXT:"did not realize the extent"] of Epstein's crimes when associating with him for philanthropy. His foundation is [USN:L8N3RG191 TEXT:"aiming to spend $200 billion"] by 2045 with an increasing focus on AI. It is working with [USN:L6N41Q1FJ TEXT:"Anthropic"] on AI-powered health checks for pregnancy, and with [USN:L6N3YL0TA TEXT:"OpenAI"] to help healthcare workers in Rwanda, Gates said. He also will speak to personnel at Anthropic and OpenAI, both of which are preparing blockbuster IPOs, about impactful giving, he said. On his mind are various ideas for addressing social upheaval. He envisioned taxing revenue from companies using “tokens” or AI's outputs to supplant labor, which could help fund a safety net. He also said society should reserve up to 40% of current jobs for humans, noting in the blog how care his dad received when suffering from Alzheimer's disease was "irreplaceably human." Gates said community protests centered on data centers were missing a bigger picture. “Wait until you really screw up the job market," he said.

item.title: La campeona olímpica de patinaje artístico Liu no competirá en la temporada 2026-27
item.description: La medallista de oro olímpica Alysa Liu anunció el martes que se perderá la próxima temporada para perfeccionar su técnica, pero aseguró a sus seguidores que volverá a la competición.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La medallista de oro olímpica Alysa Liu anunció el martes que se perderá la próxima temporada para perfeccionar su técnica, pero aseguró a sus seguidores que volverá a la competición. Liu se convirtió en la primera mujer estadounidense desde 2002 en conseguir el oro olímpico en la prueba individual femenina en los Juegos de Milán-Cortina de este año, donde también ayudó al país a conseguir el oro en la prueba por equipos. "Siempre quiero plantearme nuevos retos para que mi expresividad artística y mi patinaje puedan evolucionar", escribió Liu en una publicación en redes sociales, añadiendo que se tomaría un tiempo para "reajustarse". "Para mí es importante que mi deporte refleje mi crecimiento personal". "Así que no teman, volveré, y mientras animaré a mis compañeras de equipo, tanto a las que están cerca como a las que están lejos". En una entrevista con NBC Sports el martes, Liu dijo que tenía previsto trabajar en su "expresión artística en general, los giros, los saltos, todo" durante su descanso de la competición y que tenía la intención de volver en la temporada 2027-28. "Simplemente sentí que era lo correcto. Así que confío en mi instinto", añadió.

item.title: South African miners accelerate shift to renewable power to cut Eskom reliance
item.description: South Africa's mining firms are accelerating investment in renewable energy as they seek to diversify power sources, cut costs and meet decarbonisation targets, marking a shift after decades of reliance on state utility Eskom.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Kumwenda-Mtambo, Nelson Banya
item.content:encoded: South Africa's mining firms are accelerating investment in renewable energy as they seek to diversify power sources, cut costs and meet decarbonisation targets, marking a shift after decades of reliance on [USN:L5N3VH0N3 TEXT:"state utility Eskom"]. Anglo American (AAL.L) and Sibanye Stillwater (SSWJ.J) are among the firms reducing their dependence on a national grid dominated by [USN:L8N3UR0MY TEXT:"ageing coal-fired power plants"] that [USN:L6N3Z90DV TEXT:"has struggled"] in recent years to keep Africa's most advanced economy running. However, executives say Eskom-supplied baseload power would remain part of the energy equation for years to come even as renewable power usage grows. South Africa currently generates more than 80% of its power from coal, with renewables accounting for only around 10%. PARTNERSHIP WITH INDEPENDENT PRODUCERS Anglo is one of the companies partnering with independent power producers to develop renewable projects. In 2022 it formed a 50-50 joint venture with EDF power solutions, a subsidiary of France's EDF, to provide renewable energy to its units Kumba Iron Ore (KIOJ.J) , diamond producer De Beers and former subsidiary Valterra Platinum (VALJ.J) . The venture, Envusa Energy, currently generates 520 megawatts of power — 280 MW of wind and 240 MW of solar — representing 30% of Anglo mines' energy consumption. Its project pipeline is 1,500 MW, with ambitions to be generating 3,000 MW by 2030 for Anglo's sites and other industrial users. "You're looking at somewhere between 20% and 30% cheaper on the renewable side if you're just looking at wind and solar," Envusa CEO Nicole Mason said. "The next projects that we are focusing on are a couple of really strong wind projects as well as a number of behind-the-meter solar plus battery projects." SIBANYE FAVOURS POWER PURCHASE DEALS Sibanye, which met roughly 99% of its platinum group metals energy needs and 88% of its gold electricity demand through Eskom last year, has opted to buy renewable power through short and long-term supply deals rather than owning generation assets. It has so far contracted 835 MW of renewable energy capacity, of which 164 MW is currently operational. By the end of 2028, about 64% of total energy demand at Sibanye's South African operations is expected to be supplied from renewables, CEO Richard Stewart said, sharply cutting reliance on Eskom. "Our secured renewable energy portfolio is not only about reducing carbon emissions and enhancing energy security; it is also a business imperative that is expected to deliver meaningful cost benefits," Stewart said. He added renewable power should cost 20% to 30% less than forecast Eskom tariffs. Still, Eskom will remain crucial for the foreseeable future, Stewart said. "Renewables are intermittent by nature, battery storage technology is still developing, and Eskom supplies essential baseload power," he said. COAL MINERS EYE RENEWABLES FOR SALE Coal producers too are pushing to ramp up renewables use. Exxaro Resources (EXXJ.J) is pursuing revenue growth through its renewable energy subsidiary, Cennergi, which currently operates 297 MW of capacity and has a near-term pipeline of 593 MW. The group is targeting 1,600 MW of net installed capacity by 2030, part of a broader plan to cut scope 1 and scope 2 emissions — those produced directly by the company and from its purchased energy — by 40% by 2030 and 70% by 2040, and to reach carbon neutrality by 2050. Exxaro said a 68 MW [USN:L1N44H05G TEXT:"solar plant"] has reduced its flagship coal mine Grootegeluk's reliance on the national grid by 30%, saving the company 100 million rand ($6.25 million) annually in electricity costs and reducing scope 2 emissions by 22%. Cennergi also sells power to Eskom and other industrial users. "Our intention as part of decarbonization is that our mines could actually all go on to solar and wind energy, but obviously you still need a baseload of coal when you don't have wind or solar," CEO Ben Magara said. [USN:L1N44E045 TEXT:"Thungela Resources"] (TGAJ.J) is betting on a coal-bed methane project to diversify away from coal. Its Lephalale project aims to extract methane from coal seams in the Waterberg coalfield in Limpopo province and eventually develop a commercial liquefied natural gas business, with a timeline to be determined in part by how successfully the company uses the fuel itself. About 19 wells have been sunk at Lephalale, and the firm has begun extracting gas that will fuel a generator at one of Thungela's sites, said Chief Financial Officer Deon Smith. "For the 19 holes we are able to save 30, 40 odd million rand on the Eskom utility bill per annum if those holes are fully functional," Smith said, representing "around 6% to 7% of our total utility cost per year that we could reduce." ($1 = 16.0005 rand)

item.title: Dubai's DXB first-half passenger traffic falls more than 30% as Iran war disrupts travel
item.description: Dubai International Airport saw passenger traffic fall 31.3% in the first half of the year, its operator said on Wednesday, as the Iran war heavily disrupted traffic across the Gulf including at the busy international travel hub.
item.dc:creator: Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Dubai International Airport saw passenger traffic fall 31.3% in the first half of the year, its operator said on Wednesday, as the Iran war heavily disrupted traffic across the Gulf including at the busy international travel hub. DXB welcomed 13 million passengers in the second quarter, bringing the traffic in the first six months of the year to 31.5 million, Dubai Airports said in a statement. That compared to 46 million passengers in the same period a year earlier. Aircraft movements totalled 150,600 during the first half, down 32.1% year on year, it added. The conflict, which started on February 28, has thrown the aviation sector into turmoil this year, with flights cancelled, rescheduled and rerouted and the fallout reaching well beyond the Gulf as soaring jet fuel prices weighed on airlines globally. Middle Eastern carriers, some of the world's biggest, have seen their networks upended by the conflict, but have gradually resumed their activity. Emirates President Tim Clark said last month the airline was flying at 90% capacity. However, while more airlines are restoring flights across the Middle East, major carriers including Lufthansa, British Airways and Singapore Airlines remain cautious and have [USN:L8N43J0TW TEXT:"extended"] suspensions on a range of routes in the region. Still, Dubai Airports said the hub had shown resilience, while capacity was returning and investment continued. "The steady return of international carriers, improving connectivity and strengthening load factors signal resilient demand across key markets and growing confidence ahead of DXB's traditionally busier second half," it said. The company had [USN:L6N3Z7069 TEXT:"forecast"] passenger traffic of nearly 100 million passengers this year before the war started.

item.title: Seven charts point to tighter energy markets through 2027
item.description: The world's energy traders are sending a consistent message about 2027: They do not expect global energy markets to become calmer anytime soon.
item.dc:creator: Gavin Maguire
item.content:encoded: The world's energy traders are sending a consistent message about 2027: They do not expect global energy markets to become calmer anytime soon. With confusion still reigning over the fate of energy production and flows from the Middle East and Russia, traders are not betting on a return to the stable and predictable energy system that existed before Russia's invasion of Ukraine snarled global gas markets in 2022. From tanker freight rates and refining margins to diesel, gas and power futures, energy markets are pricing a future where geopolitical tensions remain high, supply chains remain vulnerable and key fuel products remain in short supply. FREIGHT PAIN The clearest signal comes from the routes connecting the world's biggest oil-producing region with its largest energy-consuming markets. Daily time charter rates for tankers sailing from the Middle East to China have topped $600,000 for only the second time in history, according to LSEG, as the renewed threats of an "[USN:L1N44L0FC TEXT:"economic onslaught"]" on Iran by the United States stoke concerns about fresh tensions around the Gulf. Such high rates reflect not only demand for ships, but also the risks and costs associated with moving fuels through critical maritime chokepoints. The strength of freight markets suggests traders expect disruption risks around the Gulf region to remain a feature of global energy trade well into next year. REFINED PRODUCT TENSIONS The same message is visible in refined fuel markets. Diesel futures in Europe are seen trading around 35% above their 2024-25 average through 2027, while U.S. heating oil futures, a benchmark for diesel, are currently trading about 42% above the 2024-25 average. What makes those signals notable is their consistency. Europe and North America have different refinery systems, different fuel regulations and different supply chains. Yet both markets are pricing in tight diesel supplies throughout the coming year. That suggests traders see a broader shortage of middle distillates rather than isolated regional imbalances. Asian refining markets reinforce that view. Refining margins for diesel and jet fuel in Singapore, Asia's key oil trading hub, are hovering near record highs. Refining margins represent the premium refiners receive for converting crude oil into usable fuels. High margins typically indicate that demand for products is outstripping available processing capacity. In other words, markets are not signalling an imminent shortage of crude oil. They are signalling persistent shortages of the fuels consumers actually use, and which underpin the global economy. That distinction matters. The global oil industry has expanded crude production capacity over recent years. Refining capacity has proven much harder and more expensive to replace. A wave of refinery closures in Europe and North America has reduced spare capacity, leaving fuel markets more vulnerable to disruptions in trade flows. EUROPE'S POWER WOES European energy markets are pointing to a similar conclusion. Benchmark TTF natural gas futures are seen trading around 38% above their 2024-25 average through 2027, while forward German power prices are almost 70% above the average rates for that period. Neither market is anywhere near the extraordinary highs reached during the energy crisis triggered by Russia's invasion of Ukraine . Yet neither is pricing a return to pre-crisis conditions either. Traders appear to believe Europe will continue paying a significant premium for energy security as it competes for imported gas supplies and works to balance a power system increasingly reliant on weather-dependent renewable generation. U.S. GAS STANDS ALONE The lone exception to the broader tightening story in major energy markets is U.S. natural gas. Henry Hub futures are only modestly above their recent average levels through 2027, reflecting confidence in America's ability to produce large volumes of gas even as LNG exports continue to grow. Rather than contradicting the broader message, however, U.S. gas highlights an increasingly important divide in global energy markets. North America remains one of the few regions that enjoys abundant domestic fuel supplies. Europe remains heavily dependent on imports. Asia remains exposed to disruptions in both shipping and refining. All told, the seven markets tell a coherent story. Traders are not pricing another 2022-style energy shock, or a speedy return to energy abundance. Instead, they are betting that geopolitical tensions around the Middle East, constrained refining capacity, expensive transportation and persistent competition for fuel supplies will keep energy markets tight through 2027. Or put another way, while the world's energy system looks capable of producing enough oil and gas to go around, the concern is whether those products can be refined, transported and delivered cheaply enough to meet demand. item.title: Los suizos votarán sobre si reforzar la neutralidad y poner fin a la cooperación con la OTAN
item.description: Los votantes suizos decidirán en un referéndum el próximo mes si aprueban una forma más restrictiva de neutralidad que impediría a su país imponer sanciones económicas o cooperar con la OTAN.
item.dc:creator: John Revill
item.content:encoded: Los votantes suizos decidirán en un referéndum el próximo mes si aprueban una forma más restrictiva de neutralidad que impediría a su país imponer sanciones económicas o cooperar con la OTAN. Por todo el país alpino han aparecido carteles con palomas de la paz en los que se pide a los votantes que rechacen la guerra, en una campaña que ha contado con el respaldo del Kremlin, pero que ha suscitado el temor de que pueda aislar a Suiza de sus vecinos europeos. Las encuestas de opinión sugieren que los votantes rechazarán la propuesta. Una encuesta reciente muestra un 62% en contra frente a un 36% a favor, pero, dado que los defensores del cambio están gastando más que los partidarios del statu quo, la diferencia podría reducirse, según dijo el encuestador Fabio Wasserfallen. La neutralidad suiza, reconocida internacionalmente desde 1815 e incluida en la Constitución del país desde 1848, mantuvo a Suiza al margen de ambas guerras mundiales. Sin embargo, este estatus se ve amenazado después de que Suiza impusiera sanciones a Rusia por su invasión de Ucrania en 2022, según ha declarado Christoph Blocher, un veterano político y partidario del Partido Popular Suizo, de derecha, que respalda la campaña. "Suiza no ha tenido una guerra en 200 años porque se ha mantenido permanentemente armada y neutral", dijo Blocher a Reuters en una entrevista. LOS ACTIVISTAS AFIRMAN QUE LA NEUTRALIDAD SUIZA SE ESTÁ EROSIONANDO Los términos de la neutralidad suiza no se recogen explícitamente en la Constitución. Su alcance viene definido por la Convención de La Haya de 1907, que establece que los países neutrales no deben permitir el uso militar de su territorio y deben mantenerse imparciales entre las partes beligerantes. Blocher, que ha liderado con éxito campañas en contra de una mayor integración con la Unión Europea, afirmó que la neutralidad se está viendo socavada, ya que Rusia considera ahora a Suiza parte del conflicto debido a las sanciones. "Puede que una tercera guerra mundial no esté tan lejos, y entonces importará si somos creíblemente neutrales o no", dijo. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Rusia se ha sumado al debate: la portavoz María Zajárova criticó a Suiza en una publicación en las redes sociales por alinear sus sanciones con las de la UE. "En términos jurídicos, la 'neutralidad flexible' significa que no hay neutralidad en absoluto", dijo Zajárova, quien se encuentra ella misma sujeta a sanciones suizas. La campaña pretende que la Constitución estipule que Suiza no puede adherirse ni cooperar con ninguna alianza militar o de defensa, a menos que sea atacada, y que se abstenga de sumarse a cualquier sanción a menos que esté aprobada por las Naciones Unidas. El referéndum tendrá lugar el 27 de septiembre. (1 dólar = 0,8016 francos suizos)

item.content:encoded: An overnight drone attack started a large fire at a warehouse of Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries in Russia's Tambov region, officials said on Wednesday, as Ukraine pushes ahead with its campaign to hurt the economy by targeting online retailers. Tambov Governor Evgeniy Pervyshov said about 100,000 square meters (1.1 million square feet) of the facility were set ablaze, the equivalent of 14 soccer pitches. One person was injured in the strike, he wrote on the Telegram messaging app. He did not say if the fire had been extinguished. Ukraine has been hitting Wildberries facilities since mid-July and [USN:L1N44L05J TEXT:"broadened its strategy"] in recent days to include the retailer's main rival, Ozon . The pair dominate one of the fastest-growing parts of the Russian economy, which is otherwise close to [USN:L8N43Q0O1 TEXT:"stagnation"] after 4-1/2 years of war in Ukraine. In neighbouring Lipetsk region, a man and a 14-year-old were killed in a fire lit by a falling drone, while a woman was killed in a drone attack in Belgorod region bordering Ukraine, local authorities said on Telegram. Both Ukraine and Russia have repeatedly denied targeting civilians since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022.

item.title: Sri Lanka 83-2 after India enforce follow-on
item.description: Sri Lanka reached 83-2 at lunch after India enforced the follow-on on the fourth day of the second and final test in Colombo on Wednesday. Sri Lanka still trail by 130 runs.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sri Lanka reached 83-2 at lunch after India enforced the follow-on on the fourth day of the second and final test in Colombo on Wednesday. Sri Lanka still trail by 130 runs. After declaring their first innings on 503-9, India bowled out the hosts for 290. Sri Lanka's Sonal Dinusha struck 103, his second hundred of the series, before their first innings came to an end. Mohammed Siraj dismissed Lahiru Udara (three) and Ravindra Jadeja sent back the other Sri Lanka opener Kamil Mishara (32) in their second innings. Pasindu Sooriyabandara was batting on 35 with Kamindu Mendis on 10 at the break. Siraj hurt his rib cage while trying to take a catch and walked off the field. India are 1-0 up in the two-test series.

item.title: El presidente surcoreano pide más control policial tras la polémica por las desapariciones en Jeju
item.description: El presidente de Corea del Sur, Lee Jae-myung, ha pedido una mayor rendición de cuentas por parte de la policía tras la indignación pública suscitada por la gestión de una serie de casos de desapariciones en la isla de Jeju, en un momento en el que se prevén reformas para otorgar a las fuerzas del orden un papel más destacado en las investigaciones penales.
item.dc:creator: Kyu-Seok Shim
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Corea del Sur, Lee Jae-myung, ha pedido una mayor rendición de cuentas por parte de la policía tras la indignación pública suscitada por la gestión de una serie de casos de desapariciones en la isla de Jeju, en un momento en el que se prevén reformas para otorgar a las fuerzas del orden un papel más destacado en las investigaciones penales. "Es probable que la policía sea la institución estatal que ejerza mayor poder", dijo Lee en una reunión del Consejo de Ministros celebrada el martes, y añadió que la ciudadanía se preguntaba si las fuerzas del orden podían asumir esa responsabilidad. "La responsabilidad debe reforzarse en proporción a la magnitud de la autoridad". Cuatro personas cuya desaparición se había denunciado en Jeju fueron halladas muertas en tres días, hasta el lunes, según las autoridades. Los casos no guardaban relación entre sí, pero dos de ellos habían sido supuestamente archivados por el mismo agente, sin confirmar que las personas desaparecidas estuvieran a salvo. Las acusaciones han llevado a la policía a revisar las 298 denuncias de personas desaparecidas tramitadas por dicho agente. Según medios de comunicación, se están examinando unas diez de ellas por un posible cierre indebido. Uno de los casos era el de Jang Mi-ran, una mujer de 37 años cuya desaparición se convirtió en polémica nacional después de que, supuestamente, la policía archivara el caso sin confirmar que su paradero. Su cuerpo fue hallado el lunes, 104 días después de su desaparición. El otro caso se trataba de un hombre de unos 60 años cuya familia volvió a denunciar su desaparición, lo que dio lugar a una nueva búsqueda que concluyó con el hallazgo de su cadáver. Un tribunal dictó el martes la prisión preventiva del agente, acusado de incumplimiento del deber, falsificación de registros electrónicos oficiales y obstrucción de la función pública, según la agencia de noticias Yonhap. El agente negó los cargos y dijo que se había puesto en contacto con las personas desaparecidas, según esta información, que citaba a un responsable policial. La policía de Jeju declaró a Reuters que no tenía más comentarios sobre su gestión de los casos, lo que ha avivado la preocupación por la seguridad y las críticas en las redes sociales. Yoo Jae-seong, comisario nacional de policía en funciones, se disculpó y prometió medidas para evitar que se repita la situación. La policía ha ordenado que los casos de personas desaparecidas solo se archiven con la aprobación de un superior, a la espera de una actualización de su sistema de gestión de casos, explicó Yoo a los legisladores el lunes. "Examinaremos todo el sistema y haremos mejoras institucionales para que esto no vuelva a suceder", dijo Yoo, comprometiéndose a revisar todos los casos gestionados por el agente. La policía surcoreana recibió 70.814 denuncias de adultos desaparecidos el año pasado, según datos oficiales. Desde 2022 se han presentado más de 70.000 denuncias de este tipo al año, aunque la gran mayoría se resolvieron en un plazo de 30 días, según la policía. La polémica surge después de que el Partido Democrático, en el poder, privara a los fiscales de sus restantes competencias de investigación en julio, alegando un historial de abusos. El cambio, que entrará en vigor en octubre, otorga a la policía un papel de investigación mucho más amplio.

item.title: El ministro de Exteriores de Taiwán asistirá a la cumbre de líderes de las islas del Pacífico
item.description: El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Taiwán, Lin Chia-lung, asistirá a los actos relacionados con una importante cumbre de líderes de los países insulares del Pacífico que se celebrará en Palau a partir de la próxima semana, informó el miércoles su oficina.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores de Taiwán, Lin Chia-lung, asistirá a los actos relacionados con una importante cumbre de líderes de los países insulares del Pacífico que se celebrará en Palau a partir de la próxima semana, informó el miércoles su oficina. El lanzamiento de prueba de un misil al Pacífico por parte de China en julio alarmó a las potencias regionales, pero no logró suscitar una respuesta unificada por parte de los Gobiernos de las islas del Pacífico, lo que pone de relieve las divisiones sobre cómo hacer frente a la creciente competencia estratégica en la región. China, que considera a Taiwán —gobernado democráticamente— como parte de su propio territorio, ha ido reduciendo gradualmente el número de países insulares del Pacífico que mantienen relaciones oficiales con Taipéi, de los que solo quedan tres: Palau, Tuvalu y las Islas Marshall. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Taiwán indicó que Lin partiría hacia Palau el jueves y permanecería allí una semana, participando en actos paralelos a la cumbre, entre ellos una reunión de diálogo del Foro de las Islas del Pacífico organizada por la secretaría del foro, y la Exposición sobre la Prosperidad del Pacífico. Lin se reunirá también con los aliados diplomáticos de Taiwán en el Pacífico y con "otras naciones amigas para intercambiar opiniones sobre la profundización de la colaboración entre Taiwán y las naciones insulares del Pacífico, así como sobre el mantenimiento conjunto de la paz, la estabilidad y la prosperidad en la región indopacífica", señaló el ministerio en un comunicado. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de China no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios sobre la visita de Lin a Palau con motivo del foro, que se celebra desde el domingo hasta el 4 de septiembre. China ha ampliado su influencia en el Pacífico en los últimos años mediante la financiación de infraestructuras, la expansión diplomática y la cooperación en materia de seguridad, lo que ha suscitado preocupación entre sus socios tradicionales, entre ellos Australia, Nueva Zelanda y Estados Unidos.

item.title: Al menos 15 bebés mueren en un incendio en un hospital de Islamabad, según la televisión local
item.description: Al menos 15 bebés perdieron la vida tras un incendio en un hospital público de Islamabad, la capital de Pakistán, provocado por un fallo en los sistemas de aire acondicionado, informó el miércoles la cadena local Geo TV.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Al menos 15 bebés perdieron la vida tras un incendio en un hospital público de Islamabad, la capital de Pakistán, provocado por un fallo en los sistemas de aire acondicionado, informó el miércoles la cadena local Geo TV. El incendio se inició alrededor de las 7 de la mañana (0200 GMT) en el Instituto de Ciencias Médicas de Pakistán (PIMS, por sus siglas en inglés), en la tercera planta de la unidad de salud materno-infantil del hospital, según la cadena. El incidente es uno los incendios hospitalarios más mortíferos de los últimos años en el país, donde la sanidad pública está subvencionada, pero las instalaciones carecen de recursos suficientes y están sobrecargadas, mientras que los organismos de control han criticado con frecuencia la mala gestión de los centros públicos. Había 16 recién nacidos en la unidad cuando se declaró el incendio, uno de los cuales fue rescatado, según Geo. El primer ministro, Shehbaz Sharif, ha ordenado a las autoridades que lleven a cabo una investigación inmediata, informó su oficina. "Se debe identificar a los responsables y se deben tomar las medidas más estrictas", dijo la oficina de Sharif en un comunicado. La sala fue acordonada y se vieron ambulancias fuera del edificio del hospital, según un testigo de Reuters. El PIMS, situado en el centro de Islamabad —donde el ex primer ministro Imran Khan recibió tratamiento durante un breve periodo de tiempo la semana pasada—, es uno de los principales hospitales públicos de la ciudad.

item.title: BNP Paribas et KB Kookmin en discussions pour acquérir 15% de Techcombank au Vietnam - sources
item.description: BNP Paribas et la banque sud-coréenne KB Kookmin Bank discutent séparément de l'acquisition d'au moins 15% de leur concurrent vietnamien Techcombank , dans le cadre d'une transaction dont le montant pourrait atteindre 2 milliards de dollars (1,72 milliard d'euros), selon deux sources.
item.dc:creator: Yantoultra Ngui, Phuong Nguyen
item.content:encoded: BNP Paribas (BNPP.PA) et la banque sud-coréenne KB Kookmin Bank discutent séparément de l'acquisition d'au moins 15% de leur concurrent vietnamien Techcombank (TCB.HM) , dans le cadre d'une transaction dont le montant pourrait atteindre 2 milliards de dollars (1,72 milliard d'euros), selon deux sources. L'opération, jusqu'ici non révélée, offrirait à son acquéreur un accès privilégié au marché bancaire vietnamien en forte croissance et mettrait fin à la longue quête de Techcombank d'un partenaire stratégique étranger. Techcombank vise une valorisation équivalente à environ deux fois sa valeur comptable, ont indiqué les sources, qui ont requis l'anonymat en raison du caractère confidentiel des discussions. À ce niveau de valorisation, une participation de 15% représenterait environ 2 milliards de dollars, soit une prime d'environ 55% sur le cours actuel. L'action Techcombank recule de 9% depuis le début de l'année à mardi. KB Kookmin Bank a déclaré ne pas commenter les rumeurs ou spéculations de marché, conformément aux règles sud-coréennes en matière de publication d'informations financières. Les porte-paroles de Techcombank et de BNP Paribas ont refusé de commenter. Des banques japonaises et sud-coréennes figurent déjà parmi les investisseurs stratégiques de certains des principaux établissements du pays. Le groupe japonais Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp (8316.T) a ainsi acquis une participation de 15% dans VPBank (VPB.HM) en 2023. SECTEUR BANCAIRE EN FORTE CROISSANCE La réglementation vietnamienne plafonne à 30% la participation étrangère dans la plupart des banques. Chez Techcombank, la part des investisseurs étrangers s'élève actuellement à environ 20,5% et les deux candidats envisagent plusieurs options, notamment le rachat de participations détenues par des actionnaires existants, ont indiqué les sources. Aucun accord n'a été conclu à ce stade et rien ne garantit que les discussions aboutiront, ont ajouté les sources, précisant que Techcombank ne devrait retenir qu'un seul candidat. La valorisation demeure le principal obstacle, Techcombank réclamant une prime nettement supérieure à sa valeur de marché actuelle, selon l'une des sources, qui ajoute qu'un investisseur stratégique miserait avant tout sur le potentiel de croissance futur de l'établissement. Selon les sources, un accord pourrait être conclu d'ici à fin 2026 ou au premier semestre 2027, en fonction de l'évolution des négociations. Techcombank affirme depuis longtemps être ouverte à un investisseur stratégique étranger. Elle figure parmi les rares grandes banques privées du Vietnam à ne pas disposer d'un tel partenaire. Une participation dans Techcombank offrirait un accès à l'essor de la classe moyenne vietnamienne, à la demande croissante en matière de gestion de patrimoine et au développement rapide de la banque privée dans le pays. Fondée en 1993, Techcombank comptait plus de 18 millions de clients fin 2025 et servait plus de la moitié de la clientèle vietnamienne fortunée, selon son rapport annuel 2025. Les actifs de la banque atteignaient 1.273.000 milliards de dongs (41,8 milliards d'euros) à fin juin 2026, tandis que les dépôts de clientèle s'élevaient à 697.400 milliards de dongs, selon ses états financiers. Le bénéfice avant impôt a progressé de 22,5% au premier semestre sur un an, porté par la hausse des revenus nets d'intérêts et des commissions, selon la banque.

item.title: MLB roundup: D-backs rally past Cubs on Ryan Waldschmidt's walk-off HR
item.description: Pinch hitter Ryan Waldschmidt hit a two-run walk-off homer with two outs in the ninth inning as the Arizona Diamondbacks overcame a four-run deficit to beat the Chicago Cubs 5-4 in Phoenix on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pinch hitter Ryan Waldschmidt hit a two-run walk-off homer with two outs in the ninth inning as the Arizona Diamondbacks overcame a four-run deficit to beat the Chicago Cubs 5-4 in Phoenix on Tuesday. Tim Tawa drew a walk from Jacob Webb (6-4) with one out in the ninth. Pinch runner Jose Fernandez stole second with two outs before Waldschmidt hit a 2-1 hanging slider 408 feet into the left field seats, giving the D-backs 40 comeback victories this season -- tied with the Cubs for the most in the majors. Waldschmidt is the first rookie in major league history to hit two walk-off homers while trailing in the same calendar month, also doing so Aug. 7 against the Dodgers, per OptaSTATS. The Cubs had scored 30 consecutive runs and had thrown 23 consecutive scoreless innings since falling behind the Seattle Mariners 2-0 in the second inning of a 19-2 win on Sunday until the D-backs scored three in the eighth on Tuesday. Chicago's Ian Happ hit a three-run homer off Brandon Pfaadt to break a scoreless tie in the fourth inning, his third long ball in five games. Cubs starter Clay Holmes gave up two hits, both singles, in seven scoreless innings, leaving the game with a 4-0 lead. Red Sox 7, Marlins 3 (11 innings) Jarren Duran slugged a grand slam as Boston defeated host Miami in extra innings to win its fifth straight game. Mickey Gasper homered twice for the Red Sox. He has five homers in his past eight games. Prior to that, he had no homers in 107 at-bats in the majors this season. The Marlins, who have lost two straight, were led by Heriberto Hernandez, who slugged his team-high 20th homer of the season. Both teams scored in untraditional ways in the 10th inning, Boston on a passed ball and Miami on a dropped third strike which would have otherwise been the third out and ended the game. Boston's Payton Tolle struck out seven and allowed two runs in 5 1/3 innings. Miami's Tyler Phillips lasted 4 2/3 innings, allowing one run and tying his career high with seven strikeouts. Mets 3, Brewers 2 (10 innings) Francisco Lindor homered and later scored the winning run as host New York beat Milwaukee in the opener of a three-game series. After Trevor Megill (2-3) walked Carson Benge and Luis Robert Jr., Christopher Morel hit a grounder to third which allowed automatic runner Lindor to score when David Hamilton's throw home was off-target. Jonathan Pintaro (2-0) walked one in a scoreless top of the 10th. Robert homered and had two hits for the Mets, who are 13-8 this month. Luis Lara hit a run-scoring single in the fourth and Christian Yelich delivered the game-tying, pinch-hit RBI double in the ninth for the Brewers, who have dropped two straight following a 6-1 stretch. New York rookie Zac Thornton gave up one run on seven hits over six innings. Kyle Harrison allowed one run on six hits over five innings for Milwaukee. Guardians 8, Angels 6 (10 innings) Jose Ramirez doubled three times and drove in five runs, capped by a go-ahead two-run double in the 10th inning, as Cleveland rallied from an early five-run deficit to defeat Los Angeles in Anaheim, Calif. Ramirez lined a double off Angels reliever Blake Weiman (0-1) into the gap in left-center to drive in Brayan Rocchio and Steven Kwan, leading the Guardians to their sixth straight win. Kwan went 5-for-5 with a walk, an RBI and three runs, matching his career-high hit total. Erik Sabrowski (5-2) struck out the side in the ninth, and Cade Smith fanned two during a scoreless 10th to pick up his 35th save. Vaughn Grissom hit two homers and drove in three runs, Mike Trout went 2-for-4 with a walk and a run and Christian Moore also homered for the Angels, who lost their third straight game. Pirates 1, Padres 0 Oneil Cruz lined a two-out solo homer in the top of the ninth inning to plate the only run in Pittsburgh's win over host San Diego. Cruz ripped a changeup from Mason Miller (4-2) 379 feet into the seats in right field for his 17th homer of the year and the first allowed by Miller since last August. Gregory Soto (6-4) pitched a 1-2-3 eighth inning to earn the win for the Pirates, who have won two straight against the Padres after coming into this series having lost 13 of their last 15 meetings against San Diego. Both starters pitched brilliantly but settled for no-decisions. Pittsburgh's Paul Skenes allowed just three hits in six innings, while San Diego's Michael King twirled seven innings and permitted five hits. Braves 4, Dodgers 3 Ozzie Albies hit a go-ahead RBI single in the eighth inning and Raisel Iglesias pitched around Shohei Ohtani's leadoff triple in the ninth as Atlanta held on to beat visiting Los Angeles. After Ohtani's triple, Iglesias struck out Freddie Freeman and got Mookie Betts to ground out. After Max Muncy was intentionally walked, Tommy Edman flied out to center field, preserving Atlanta's second straight win and ending the Dodgers' six-game winning streak. Braves starter Bryce Elder threw six innings of three-run, eight-hit ball while Los Angeles starter Tyler Glasnow, making his first start since May 6 after dealing with back issues, went five innings and allowed three runs on six hits with seven strikeouts. Astros 9, Yankees 7 Yainer Diaz homered twice, Yordan Alvarez hit a tiebreaking RBI triple with two outs in the eighth inning and Houston outlasted host New York. Diaz started the deciding three-run rally off Brent Headrick (7-3) by homering to right with one out to tie the game 6-6. After a single by Jeremy Pena, Alvarez roped a first-pitch slider to the warning track in right-center field before scoring on a single by Isaac Paredes. Spencer Jones doubled and Jazz Chisholm Jr. singled him home to kick off the bottom of the eighth but Bryan Abreu (5-3) got Austin Wells to ground into a double play and Josh Hader finished it off by notching the final four outs for his 19th save in 19 chances. White Sox 11, Rangers 7 Tristan Peters delivered a two-run double during a six-run first inning and homered for the fourth straight game as host Chicago held off Texas. Chicago evened the series between American League playoff contenders at one game apiece. The White Sox out-hit the Rangers 14-11, but needed a ninth-inning escape despite their strong start as Grant Taylor came on with the bases loaded and two out to get Cody Freeman to ground into a forceout at second to end the game. Rangers starter Jacob deGrom allowed the first five batters of the game to reach base. deGrom (9-9) went only 3 2/3 innings, giving up eight runs. Chicago left-hander Anthony Kay benefited from the early run support but fell one out short of qualifying for the victory after giving up four runs over 4 2/3 innings. Mariners 4, Phillies 1 Cal Raleigh homered and George Kirby pitched 7 2/3 strong innings as Seattle defeated visiting Philadelphia for a fourth win in five games. Kirby (9-10) allowed one run on six hits and a walk while striking out nine. Mariners closer Andres Munoz worked the ninth for his 24th save of the season. Raleigh, who went deep three times on Monday, tied the team record of four homers in as many at-bats. Bryce Harper had two hits for the Phillies, who have lost two in a row after a nine-game winning streak. Aaron Nola (5-10) permitted two runs on three hits in six innings. Royals 5, Blue Jays 3 Salvador Perez knocked in the go-ahead run with a fifth-inning single and Kansas City held off host Toronto for its ninth straight victory. The game ended when Toronto's Nathan Lukes was thrown out at second trying to stretch his two-run single off Steven Cruz into a double. Left fielder Isaac Collins got the ball to shortstop Bobby Witt Jr., whose throw to second got Lukes. Kansas City starter Seth Lugo (6-7) allowed one run on six hits and one walk with five strikeouts in five innings, while Toronto's Max Scherzer (1-7) allowed two runs in five innings as he dropped a seventh straight decision. Rockies 3, Nationals 1 Hunter Goodman homered in his return from the injured list as Colorado snapped a seven-game losing streak with a win at Washington. The Rockies, who entered the game with the fourth-highest bullpen ERA in the majors (4.88), got five innings of scoreless relief from relievers. Mark Manfredi (1-0) pitched one inning for his first big league win and Jordan Romano worked the ninth for his 13th save. The Nationals lost for the ninth time in 11 games. Washington went 0-for-6 with runners in scoring position and totaled five hits one night after scoring 13 runs on 13 hits. Mason Adams started for Colorado and pitched four innings in his major league debut. Orioles 13, Cardinals 1 Pete Alonso went 4-for-4 with a three-run home run and Christian Encarnacion-Strand also homered and drove in three runs as Baltimore hammered host St. Louis. Jackson Holliday added three hits and right-hander Chris Bassitt pitched effectively into the seventh inning for the Orioles, who remain in the thick of a crowded AL wild-card race despite being four games under .500. Alonso's 31st homer of the season keyed a four-run third inning and Encarnacion-Strand's seventh homer capped it. Bassitt (5-4) gave the Orioles a boost in his third start back since having surgery in June to remove bone spurs from his back, allowing a run on six hits (five singles) over 6 2/3 innings. Tigers 4, Rays 1 Max Clark hit his second career home run to help propel host Detroit to a victory over Tampa Bay which ended its six-game losing streak. Javier Baez scored two runs and Hao-Yu Lee added an RBI single for the Tigers. Detroit starter Jackson Jobe gave up one run in 4 1/3 innings. Drew Sommers (1-3) didn't allow a baserunner in 1 2/3 innings while picking up his first major league win. Kenley Jansen got the last three outs to record his 17th save. Bulk Rays reliever Ian Seymour (9-5) gave up all four runs -- three earned -- and seven hits in the final 5 2/3 innings. Junior Caminero had two hits and scored the lone run for the AL East leaders, who scored first in the fourth. Jonny DeLuca had the lone RBI. Athletics 4, Twins 2 Carlos Cortes hit a two-run homer and Gage Jump pitched into the seventh inning as the Athletics beat Minnesota in West Sacramento, Calif. Lawrence Butler had two hits for the Athletics, who won for the third time in four games. Jump (6-8) allowed two runs on three hits over 6 1/3 innings. Hogan Harris recorded two outs, Luis Medina pitched a scoreless eighth inning and Elvis Alvarado retired the Twins in order in the ninth for his fourth save. Royce Lewis had two of the Twins' four hits. Minnesota struck out 12 times and lost for the fourth time in five games. Right-hander Taj Bradley (9-6) threw the first immaculate inning (three strikeouts on nine total pitches) in Twins history in the fifth inning but allowed four runs on seven hits over 6 2/3 innings. Giants 3, Reds 1 Rafael Devers homered again, another pitcher got injured early in his start, and San Francisco followed a winning -- albeit painful -- script to beat visiting Cincinnati. One night after they built an early lead and lost starting pitcher Carson Whisenhunt to an elbow injury, the Giants repeated the pattern. Adrian Houser exited due to arm tightness in the second inning, and he will undergo an MRI on Wednesday. Anthony Molina (1-0) threw 4 1/3 innings to win his Giants debut. Carson Seymour was credited with his first career save despite serving up a Sal Stewart homer in the ninth. San Francisco's Drew Cavanaugh had three hits and two RBIs. --Field Level Media

item.title: Hyundai lifts margin target, expands US hybrid lineup
item.description: Hyundai Motor said on Wednesday it would launch or refresh more than 100 vehicles globally by 2030 and expand its U.S. hybrid lineup, as the South Korean automaker seeks to lift its operating profit margin above 9%.
item.dc:creator: Heekyong Yang, Heejin Kim
item.content:encoded: Hyundai Motor (005380.KS) said on Wednesday it would launch or refresh more than 100 vehicles globally by 2030 and expand its U.S. hybrid lineup, as the South Korean automaker seeks to lift its operating profit margin above 9%. Under what it described as its largest-ever product rollout, Hyundai plans to introduce 58 models in North America by 2030, as it seeks to gain share in vehicle segments where it has limited presence and fend off growing competition. It is a "product offensive across every region," Hyundai said in a statement as it held its 2026 CEO investor day in Seoul on Wednesday, adding that it was also targeting "white spaces" where its brand is underrepresented today. "These segments account for roughly 29% of all automotive sales, highlighting significant opportunities for growth." Shares of Hyundai Motor were 3.3% lower after the announcements, lagging a 1.3% rise in the broader market (.KS11) , as it maintained a shareholder return ratio of at least 35% of its net profit. HYBRID EXPANSION Hyundai said it would add 1.27 million units of new global capacity by 2030, including 500,000 units in North America. "Our fundamentals have never been stronger," CEO Jose Munoz said, pointing to Hyundai Motor Group's global position. Hyundai Motor, together with affiliate Kia (000270.KS) , is the world's third-largest automaker by sales. It plans to introduce 10 hybrid models in North America by 2030 and the company said hybrids would reach half of regional sales there. The push comes as higher gasoline prices linked to the Iran war have strengthened demand for fuel-efficient vehicles, particularly hybrids. Some 56% of U.S. car shoppers said rising gasoline prices made them more likely to consider a hybrid, according to Cox Automotive data, while hybrid sales rose 19% in the first half of 2026, according to Omdia. Hyundai's hybrid sales climbed 71% in the second quarter. However, Hyundai's U.S. expansion also faces trade policy risk from the ongoing review of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), which governs duty-free access for vehicles and parts moving across North America. U.S. officials have declined to extend the agreement automatically, raising the prospect of annual reviews and less certainty for capital-intensive investment plans that depend on cross-border supply chains. ROBOTICS Hyundai also outlined plans to broaden its businesses, including robotics, autonomous driving and robotaxis. It said deliveries of IONIQ 5 vehicles to Alphabet's Waymo for use as robotaxis would begin in the fourth quarter of 2026. Hyundai's Motional venture is also due to launch driverless commercial services later this year, initially in Las Vegas. The automaker said it would begin U.S. production of robots in 2028, targeting annual capacity of 30,000 units. It plans to deploy Boston Dynamics' Atlas humanoid robot at its Georgia Metaplant from 2028. Hyundai is testing how humanoid robots could be used in car production at a facility in Georgia that replicates factory floor conditions. Hyundai said it would raise its 2030 consolidated operating margin target from the 8%-9% range previously forecast to above 9%, while keeping its 2026 margin guidance at 6.3%-7.3%. Hyundai also reaffirmed a target of 5.55 million global vehicle sales by 2030, equivalent to a 6% market share, and said electrified vehicles would account for 60% of sales by then, compared with 23% in 2025.
